title: Federico III of Naples to the Catholic Monarchs, San Germano, 11 Jan 1497, in Joan Ram Escrivà's cipher no. 1: BnF Espagnol 318 no. 5, ff. 5-6v (catalogue item 9)

system.summary: The cipher issued to Joan Ram Escrivà, Spanish ambassador at Naples (Escrivà no. 1; Parisi 2004 app. II): a sign alphabet with a nomenclator of letter groups with initials p, q, r, s, t, v, x (qav de, vee que, xer/xoq Vuestras Altezas ...).
system.notes: Split on 14 Oct 2026 from esp318 (the whole volume) under the one-key rule. The other ciphered letters of Espagnol 318 have their own entries: esp318 (no. 92), esp318no95, esp318no93.

prior_solution.where: Parisi 2020 (open access, DOI 10.54103/2611-318X/14378): identification of the cipher and the whole Italian text

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Mapped the five ciphered letters of Espagnol 318 from the manifest and notice; no. 5 is ff. 5-6v (canvases 32-35).
Searching the shelfmark found Parisi 2020, who identified the cipher as Escrivà's and printed the whole letter; the nomenclator groups he lists were checked against the leaf at 3000 px and match.

Split from the former whole-volume target esp318 under the one-key rule (George Lasry, 14 Oct 2026): no. 5 is in Escrivà's cipher, a different key from the other ciphered letters of the volume. Own folder, profile, page and ledgers.
Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): decryption = Parisi 2020 linked by DOI (modern article, not copied); no ciphertext transcription exists (project work).

Parisi's printed text (2020, pp. 173-174, read in targets/esp318/lit/parisi2020.txt and in the article PDF fetched again from riviste.unimi.it) translated into English, sentence for sentence (texts/no5_en.md); the limits of the cipher part taken from the leaf (clear to 'me havea declarato', clear again from 'Et perché longamente').

Opened f. 5r (targets/esp318/full/f005r.jpg) to transcribe the cipher: about 22 lines of graphic signs with Latin-letter nomenclator groups, a stain down the middle; the sign table of Parisi 2004 survives in the repository only as text without its glyphs. Not transcribed; recorded as transcription_missing.

texts.label: Esp. 318 no. 5, Federico III to the Catholic Monarchs, 11 Jan 1497
texts.summary: Federico III of Naples to Ferdinand and Isabella, San Germano, 11 Jan 1497, enciphered by the Spanish ambassador Joan Ram Escrivà in his own cipher: Federico confirms the pre-agreement for the marriage of his nine-year-old son Ferrando, duke of Calabria, to one of the Spanish infantas.
texts.note: The whole letter is printed by Ivan Parisi (2020, Studi di storia medioevale e di diplomatica n.s. IV, pp. 157-177, open access; the text is on pp. 173-174), a modern publication: linked by DOI, not copied. The translation (14 Nov 2026) is of his printed text. No transcription of the ciphertext: see transcription_missing; the scans are in targets/esp318/full/.
texts.transcription_missing: The cipher on f. 5r (about 22 lines, scan in targets/esp318/full/f005r.jpg, opened again on 14 Nov 2026) is written in graphic signs of Escrivà's homophonic alphabet with Latin-letter nomenclator groups (qix, qao, vee ...), and a stain down the middle of the leaf covers part of every line. The sign table (Parisi 2004, Pedralbes 24, appendix II, 'Alfabeto n. 1') is in the repository only as extracted text (targets/garcilaso1498/lit/parisi2004.txt), where the glyphs are lost, so a faithful transcription needs a sign inventory first, which was not built in this pass. To unblock: the printed alphabet table of Parisi 2004, then a line-by-line transcription checked on Parisi's 2020 text.
